new.title: Taste fresh organic cheese at the Hafenkäserei
new.desc: The Hafenkäserei is an organic show dairy on the south side of Münster's Stadthafen, where cheese production can be watched live. It combines a restaurant and café over two floors with a terrace facing the harbour basin.
new.tip: Try the cheese tasting or a fondue evening; check the current opening hours and book ahead for evenings. The terrace is best on a dry day.

new.title: Drink single-origin coffee at the roestbar Kreuzviertel
new.desc: The roestbar opened its first café on Nordstraße in 2003 and roasts its beans in-house on a machine called Molly. The company was named best roastery in North Rhine-Westphalia by the magazine Feinschmecker for 2025.
new.tip: Open roughly 9 to 18 on weekdays and 10 to 18 on Sundays. Order a filter coffee or espresso from the house blend, the Münster Mischung.

new.title: Try a Finne organic beer at the Viertelbrauerei
new.desc: Finne is a Münster craft brewery with its Viertelbrauerei in the Kreuzviertel and a second brewery at the harbour since 2025. The beers are brewed organically and served in the brewery taproom.
new.tip: Check opening days before going, as taproom hours vary. A tasting flight is a good way to sample the range.

new.title: Have cake at the farm café of Nahrup's Hof in Greven
new.desc: Nahrup's Hof is a family asparagus farm at Postdamm in Greven, with a farm shop and a café with a farm-estate atmosphere. Regional products and animal enclosures round out the visit.
new.tip: The café is mainly open at weekends, roughly Saturday afternoon and Sunday from 9; confirm times first. It is a good stop on a cycle ride through the Münsterland.

new.title: Eat Westphalian farm cooking at Hof Grothues-Potthoff
new.desc: Hof Grothues-Potthoff in Senden is a family farm with a farm shop, bakery, pastry shop, restaurant and hotel. Its café and restaurant serve Westphalian dishes made with produce from the farm.
new.tip: The café is listed as open daily, with longer hours on Sundays. The farm shop is the place to buy bread and regional products to take home.

new.title: Buy spelt and emmer spirits at Gerbermann in Alverskirchen
new.desc: Gerbermann is a small distillery in Alverskirchen that makes spirits from spelt and emmer grown on its own land. It sells them through its own farm shop and in local restaurants.
new.tip: Visit the farm shop for bottles to take home; call ahead for opening times. It is a short detour from the Everswinkel cycle routes.

new.title: Walk around the moated Burg Gemen
new.desc: Burg Gemen in Borken-Gemen is a moated castle first mentioned in 1092, with the oldest parts about 900 years old. Its present size was reached by 1411. Since 1946 the Diocese of Münster has used it as a youth education centre, the Jugendburg Gemen.
new.tip: The grounds suit walks toward the Sternbusch; the castle is not a regular museum, so view it from outside and check for events. No parking on the castle grounds, use Coesfelder Straße.

new.title: Stroll the grounds of the baroque Schloss Ahaus
new.desc: Schloss Ahaus was a summer palace of the Prince-Bishops of Münster. The complex houses the Torhausmuseum and the Westphalian School Museum, and the park is part of Ahaus's town parks.
new.tip: The exterior and park can be seen at any time; check museum opening times before visiting inside.

new.title: Visit the Ludgerus-Dom in Billerbeck
new.desc: The St.-Ludgerus-Dom, known as the Baumberge cathedral, stands in the middle of Billerbeck. It is a pilgrimage church tied to St. Ludger, first bishop of Münster, who died in Billerbeck in 809.
new.tip: Entry is free outside services. Combine it with a walk through the old town and the Baumberge hills.

new.title: Explore the kult Westmünsterland museum in Vreden
new.desc: The kult replaced the old Hamaland-Museum and opened in July 2017. It combines the regional museum with the Kreisarchiv and the Vreden town archive under one roof, with exhibitions on culture and tradition in the western Münsterland.
new.tip: The address is Kirchplatz 14 in the town centre; check current opening hours.

new.title: Walk the castle park of Schloss Senden
new.desc: Schloss Senden is a moated baroque castle in the town of Senden, surrounded by a public castle park. It is a short ride from Münster.
new.tip: The park is open to walkers; the castle itself is private, so view it from the park.
